answer: Every payout passes a narrow jetty that admits one claim per funding trail per epoch, so extra clones queue. Each claim must carry a fresh pigment, a dye mixed from the hash of a stranger-commissioned job, and every pigment is stamped in the public sable ledger, where any reused or near-identical pigment burns both claims. Fielding n clones therefore needs n stranger jobs, n pigments, and queue fees that double each epoch waited, while the prize per trail is fixed and split n ways, so cloning costs n times the work for 1/n of the reward.
